problem_type: Anchored popover Escape continues into host keyboard commands
symptom: Closing the canvas node effect picker with Escape also deselects the node, so the node composer disappears.
direct_cause: AnchoredPopover initially mounts its portal at visibility:hidden, so the requested child autoFocus is rejected and focus remains on the external trigger. Escape bubbles from that button through React Flow's NodeWrapper, which deselects the node before AnchoredPopover's document-bubble listener closes the picker.
class_root: AnchoredPopover does not arbitrate Escape between its anchor, portal, delegated child layers and the React Flow keyboard boundary, so one key can both close an overlay and deselect its node.
affected_population: Keyboard users of every AnchoredPopover consumer, including canvas node effects and storyboard composer overflow controls
Anchored popovers whose focus is on an external anchor, a portal button, a portal input, or a nested popup control
entry_points: Escape from content rendered in the AnchoredPopover portal
Escape delegated first to a nested popup or composing input
Escape outside the popover retained by the existing document fallback
internal_only_reason: The ownership invariant belongs to Nomi's shared AnchoredPopover. Installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5 source was inspected to confirm that NodeWrapper validly maps unowned Escape to node deselection; no dependency defect or API change is required.
invariants: An open AnchoredPopover consumes ordinary close, composing, and child-prevented Escape at its anchor or portal; delegated child Escape may continue to document but cannot deselect its React Flow node.
A composing event, a child-prevented event, an open nested popup, or a higher dialog keeps first refusal and does not close the parent popover or deselect its React Flow node.
The existing document fallback still closes an open AnchoredPopover when focus is outside both the anchor and portal.
React Flow retains its normal Escape-to-deselect behavior when no AnchoredPopover owns the event.

door_reduction.why_not: The five production consumers (node effects, storyboard overflow, transition picker, asset picker and project sync badge) plus the design-lab specimen remain valid distinct presentations. They converge on AnchoredPopover, so fixing its one event boundary covers every door without removing features or duplicating ownership in callers.

generality_proof: The shared component receives every anchor reference, renders every portal layer, and already owns the document fallback. It consumes ordinary local Escape before React ancestors, marks the open anchor and portal with React Flow's installed .nokey boundary for delegated child events, and snapshots overlayLayers ownership before child teardown for every consumer.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Arbitrate Escape once across the external anchor, portal content, nested popup, IME, and focus-outside fallback before invoking onClose.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Its close callback synchronously returns focus to an anchor inside React Flow; the real desktop probe recorded that anchor as the Escape target and NodeWrapper deselected before document bubble.
It also returns focus synchronously to its external dots anchor and contains nested NomiSelect popups, exercising the same anchor/portal/nested ownership class outside React Flow.
It delegates Escape closure to the same AnchoredPopover boundary and therefore receives the same single-command guarantee without caller logic.

recurrence.reason: The shared component has multiple anchors and portal content types, and any current or future ancestor may bind Escape independently. The missing ownership rule is reusable and not specific to the effect picker.
same_class_scan: rg AnchoredPopover found five production consumers plus the design-lab specimen, all converging on src/design/AnchoredPopover.tsx.
NodeEffectChips and ShotComposerBar independently restore focus to external anchors; ShotComposerBar additionally contains nested NomiSelect portals.
Installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5 NodeWrapper maps unowned Escape to unselect, while isInputDOMNode only protects input-like event targets.

prevention.invariant: Escape owned by an open anchored popover stack cannot deselect its React Flow node; local child, nested-popup, higher-dialog, and IME ownership remains first.
prevention.failure_mode: The boundary stops ordinary parent-close events, lets delegated child events reach their document handlers behind React Flow's .nokey guard, and leaves unowned React Flow Escape unchanged after cleanup.
prevention.strategy: Use one shared Escape arbiter from the anchor target, portal React boundary, and existing document fallback, reusing overlayLayers for nested ownership and removing the old close-only document logic.

legacy_paths.rationale: The close-only document Escape handler is replaced in place by the shared ownership arbiter; no parallel caller or fallback implementation remains.

dependency_lifecycle.target: Retain the pinned version; on any React Flow upgrade, verify or replace the installed isInputDOMNode .nokey contract before adoption.
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: React Flow's Escape-to-deselect behavior is correct when the node owns the key. The installed @xyflow/system isInputDOMNode explicitly exempts targets inside .nokey before NodeWrapper handles Escape; AnchoredPopover uses that narrow framework boundary while open so a nested document-bubble owner can still receive the original event.
exit_criteria: The candidate @xyflow/system source still makes NodeWrapper ignore keyboard events whose composed-path target is inside .nokey, or Nomi replaces this use with a documented equivalent exposed by that release.
tests/ux/composerLifecycle.test.mjs passes anchor, portal button, document-bubble child, higher-dialog, cleanup, and ordinary unowned React Flow Escape cases on the candidate version.

migration: No persisted data or caller migration is required. Existing onClose callbacks and anchor refs retain their signatures and converge on the repaired shared boundary.
residual_risks: The focused browser harness covers Chromium and real React portal behavior; platform-specific native IME composition remains verified through the KeyboardEvent isComposing contract rather than a live OS candidate window.
React Flow exposes .nokey in installed runtime source rather than a configurable public prop; the dependency exit criteria and real NodeWrapper regression make a future rename fail visibly.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Every anchored popover consumer converges on this design-system boundary, and the real browser harness mounts it under React Flow with anchor, portal, nested-popup, IME, fallback, and unowned Escape paths.
